decisions.decision: Retries live in the transport layer (withRetry, with backoff). API callers call request() once and never wrap it in their own retry loop; tune retries through request()'s retry option.
decisions.author: Jeremy Barnes

decisions.decision: Code under src/ logs through logger from src/lib/logger.ts, never console.*, so logs stay structured JSON. console is fine in scripts/.
decisions.author: Priya Natarajan

decisions.decision: Every HTTP call goes through request() in src/api/client.ts, which adds the base URL, the timeout, retries and the Result wrapping; client.ts is the only file that calls fetch.
decisions.author: Jeremy Barnes

decisions.decision: SQL in src/db is written only with the q`` tagged template, so every value becomes a parameter. Never build statement text with string concatenation or plain template strings.
decisions.author: Sam Okafor

decisions.decision: Only src/config.ts reads process.env. Every other module imports config; a new setting is a new field in Config.
decisions.author: Priya Natarajan

decisions.decision: Components in src/ui are named exports, never export default, so imports match the component name and src/ui/index.ts can re-export them.
decisions.author: Lena Fischer

decisions.decision: Every date shown in src/ui is formatted by formatDate or another helper in src/lib/format.ts, so all screens share one format and time zone.
decisions.author: Lena Fischer

decisions.decision: API functions in src/api return failures as Result values (err(...)) and never throw, so the caller decides what to show.
decisions.author: Jeremy Barnes

decisions.decision: Components in src/ui don't compute totals, VAT or shipping; that logic lives in src/lib (pricing.ts has orderTotals) and components render what they get.
decisions.author: Lena Fischer

decisions.decision: Request handlers in src/routes parse their input with a zod schema declared next to the handler, like UpdateUserBody in src/routes/users.ts.
decisions.author: Sam Okafor

distractors.decision: Name new files in kebab-case, except React components in src/ui, which are PascalCase like the component they export.
Import types with `import type` when a module is used only for its types.
Prefer early returns to nested if/else blocks.
Array parameters a function does not mutate are typed readonly.
Money is an integer number of cents everywhere; never a float of euros.
Ids are opaque strings: never parse them or compare their prefixes (u_, o_).
Use unknown rather than any, and narrow it before use.
Prefer const; use let only for values that are reassigned.
Write a doc comment on an exported function only when its name does not say what it does.
Rounding in src/lib uses Math.round on integer cents, never toFixed.
src/lib never imports React; UI-only helpers live in src/ui.
Every id interpolated into an API path goes through encodeURIComponent.
Query strings are built with URLSearchParams, not by joining strings by hand.
An endpoint's request and response types live next to the function that calls it.
Test names describe behaviour ("returns…", "refuses…"), not the function under test.
Test files mirror the source path: src/lib/x.ts is tested in test/lib/x.test.ts.
Repository functions in src/db are named for what they return (ordersForUser), not how (selectOrders).
Row types in src/db keep the columns' snake_case names; mapping to camelCase happens at the API boundary.
A component's props interface is named <Component>Props and exported next to it.
Style components with className strings, not inline style objects.
Every <button> in src/ui has an explicit type attribute.
Components call hooks at the top level, before any early return.
Handlers answer errors as JSON { error } with the matching HTTP status.
Durations are milliseconds, and names say so with an Ms suffix (timeoutMs).
Error codes are stable snake_case strings (order_not_found); messages may change, codes may not.
Exported names are spelled out (orderCount, not ordCnt).
Scripts exit non-zero on failure and print a one-line summary when they finish.
Migrations are named YYYYMMDDHHMM_description.sql and never edited once merged.
An issued invoice is never changed; corrections are credit notes.
Tax rates in billing come from the tax table, keyed by country and date, never hard-coded.
Every admin action is written to the audit log with the acting user's id.
Admin permissions are checked on the server; the UI only hides controls.
Each package declares its own dependencies and never imports another package's src/ directly.
Packages publish ESM only, with an exports map.
Background jobs are idempotent: running one twice changes nothing more than running it once.
Jobs take a cursor and process at most 500 rows per run.
Passwords are hashed with argon2id.
Session cookies are HttpOnly, Secure and SameSite=Lax.
Email templates are plain functions returning { subject, html, text }.
Search indexing happens asynchronously, through the jobs queue.
Cache keys start with the entity and a version: user:v2:<id>.
Every new design-system component has a story next to it.
Icon-only buttons in src/ui carry an aria-label that names the action.
Every in src/ui has alt text; decorative images use an empty alt.
Component tests find elements by role or label text, never by data-testid.
Icons come from the shared icon set in src/ui/icons; no inline SVG markup inside components.
Interactive elements keep a visible focus outline; an outline is never removed without a replacement.
Colours come from the theme tokens, never hex literals written in a component.
Margins and paddings stay on the 4px spacing scale: 4, 8, 12, 16, 24 or 32.
Button labels and headings use sentence case: "Save changes", not "Save Changes".
A component file exports one component; the small helper components it needs stay unexported in that file.
List items get a stable key taken from the data, never the array index.
Form inputs are controlled components; values are never read back through refs.
Event props are named on<Event>, and the functions that handle them handle<Event>.
Boolean props read as adjectives (disabled, compact), never isX or hasX.
When a component destructures its props, children comes last.
Modals render through the shared Dialog component, never their own createPortal call.
Tooltips never repeat text that is already visible: they explain, they do not label.
Text that can overflow truncates with an ellipsis and keeps its full value in a title attribute.
z-index values come from the layers map in the theme, never raw numbers.
Animations respect prefers-reduced-motion and last at most 200 ms.
Navigation uses links and actions use buttons; a button never changes the URL.
While a request a control started is pending, that control is disabled so it cannot be sent twice.
Date inputs use the shared DatePicker; never a native input of type date.
Components read feature flags through the useFlag hook, never straight from the flags config.
A component is wrapped in memo only for a measured reason, written in a comment above it.
A React context holds one concern; state and its setters go in two separate contexts.
JSX never nests ternaries; extract a component or return early instead.
Fragments use the short <>…</> syntax unless they need a key.
A component file reads top to bottom: imports, types, the component, then its local helpers.
Components never spread unknown props onto DOM elements.
Numeric text fields use inputMode="numeric" rather than type="number".
Each screen has exactly one h1; the sections under it use h2 and h3 in order.
Icons are 16 or 24 pixels; any other size is agreed with the design team first.
Counts in interface copy are written as digits: "3 orders", not "three orders".
Plurals go through the plural() helper, never a hand-written "s" suffix.
Nothing is reachable by hover alone; every hover action also has a click and a keyboard path.
Components never set the document's scroll position themselves; they use the useScrollTo hook.
Conditional class names are joined with the cx helper, never with template strings.
Every dialog has a title, and its close button is the first focusable element.
Shared components export their props type so stories and tests can build fixtures from it.
API functions are named verb then noun: getOrder, listUsers, updateUser.
Each file in src/api covers one resource; calls that combine resources live in src/services.
Types for raw API payloads end in Dto and are mapped to domain types before leaving src/api.
An API function takes an options object rather than more than two positional parameters.
Values returned from src/api are typed readonly.
HTTP header names are written in lowercase.
Request body types are named after their action with a Request suffix, like UpdateUserRequest.
Each API function's doc comment names the HTTP method and the path it calls.
API functions never touch local storage, cookies or the DOM.
Ids passed to API functions use the branded OrderId and UserId types, not plain strings.
Query cache keys for API calls are built by the keys helper in src/api/keys.ts.
Status values from the API are string unions, never TypeScript enums.
Dates sent to the API are ISO 8601 strings in UTC.
Boolean query parameters are sent as true or false, never 1 or 0.
API types use null for absent values the server sends, and undefined only for optional inputs.
Array fields, and functions that return arrays, have plural names.
src/api holds functions only: no classes and no singletons.
An API file stays under 300 lines; it splits by sub-resource when it grows past that.
Every type an API function's signature uses is exported from the same file.
A deprecated API function carries an @deprecated tag that names its replacement.
When an API function takes an id, the id is its first parameter.
Renames from snake_case payload fields happen in one mapper per resource.
API responses are never cast through any; they are typed with their Dto.
Sort parameters are sent as sort=field:asc or sort=field:desc.
An API function's name matches the operation id of the server route it calls.
Values an API function returns get a specific name, never data, result or response.
Endpoints that take many ids receive them as one comma-separated ids parameter, never repeated keys.
Calls that need only a few fields ask for them with the fields parameter.
Timestamp columns end in _at and date-only columns end in _on.
Table names are plural snake_case; join tables name both sides, like order_tags.
New tables use uuid primary keys generated by the database.
Indexes are named idx_<table>_<columns>.
Repository functions return plain objects, never the driver's row types.
Pool limits are set once in the database config, never passed per query.
Every schema change in src/db ships with a down step in the same change.
Each repository has one rowTo<Entity> mapper; queries never shape result objects inline.
Enum-like columns use a CHECK constraint, not a Postgres enum type.
JSON columns are typed with a named type declared next to the repository that reads them.
Repositories import the pool from connection.ts; no repository creates its own client.
There is one repository file per aggregate root, named <entity>-repo.ts.
Every table has a COMMENT ON TABLE saying what one row is.
Repositories export plain functions, not a repository object or class.
Count queries return a number, never the driver's string count.
Timestamps are stored as timestamptz, in UTC.
Boolean columns are named is_<adjective> or has_<noun>.
Repository tests build their rows with the factories in test/factories.
A repository holds no state between requests; every function takes what it needs.
Functions in src/lib do no I/O of any kind.
src/lib exports functions and types, never classes.
Helpers are named for what they return, not how they work: orderTotals, not computeStuff.
Helpers take at most three positional arguments; anything more goes in an options object.
Helpers never mutate their inputs; they return new objects and arrays.
Dates parsed from strings go through parseIsoDate, which rejects anything that is not ISO 8601.
Default parameter values are literals only, never function calls.
Helpers avoid function overloads; they take a union parameter or become two functions.
Every exported helper's doc comment has one @example.
A src/lib module exports only what other folders use; its internal helpers stay private.
Helpers in src/lib take their settings as parameters and never import the app's config module.
Type guards are named is<Type> and live next to the type they check.
Recursive helpers carry an explicit depth limit.
Nothing in src/lib knows about HTTP: no request or response types.
Generic type parameters get descriptive names like TItem, not single letters beyond T.
Helpers that only iterate accept an Iterable<T> rather than an array.
Helpers return undefined, not null, when there is no result.
src/lib has no index.ts barrel; callers import from the module file itself.
Async helpers carry no Async suffix; their Promise return type says it.
Handlers are named <verb><Resource>Handler, like listOrdersHandler.
In a handler that needs a user, the auth check is the first statement.
Handlers stay under 30 lines; anything longer moves to src/services.
Handlers take the framework's Request type and return a Response; no custom wrappers.
CORS headers are set by middleware, never inside a handler.
Public routes declare their rate limit in the route table.
GET handlers set Cache-Control explicitly, even when it is no-store.
Route files export a routes array listing each handler's method and path.
A breaking change to a route gets a new path; the old path keeps working for one release.
Handlers never set the Date header; the server adds it.
TODO comments name an owner and a ticket: TODO(alice, ORD-123).
Comments say why the code is the way it is, not what it does.
Source files stay under 400 lines.
Boolean variables read as questions: isReady, hasLines.
Tests follow arrange, act, assert, with a blank line between the three.
No snapshot tests: assert on the values that matter.
Tests that depend on time use fake timers, never real waits.
Each test checks one behaviour, and its name says which.
Property access on maybe-missing values uses optional chaining, not && chains.
No TypeScript enums anywhere; string unions instead.
Exported functions declare their return type.
A switch over a union ends with an exhaustiveness check.
A string literal used in more than one place becomes a named constant.
Scripts that write data take a --dry-run flag and run dry unless told otherwise.
Scripts parse their arguments with parseArgs from node:util.
Tool config files carry a comment saying why each non-default option is set.
Plan changes are prorated to the day, never refunded in full.
Failed renewals are retried on days 1, 3 and 7; after that the account is paused.
Impersonating a user needs a reason, stored with the audit entry.
Bulk admin actions ask for the number of affected rows to be typed back before running.
Each job declares its retry policy in its definition, with a dead-letter queue after the last attempt.
Job names are <domain>.<verb>, like orders.reindex.
Sessions expire after 14 days without activity.
Changing an email address or password needs a fresh second factor.
Every email has a plain-text part written by hand, not generated from the HTML.
Marketing emails carry a one-click unsubscribe header.
Search synonyms live in one synonyms file that support reviews.
Every cache entry has a TTL; nothing is cached forever.
Translation keys are dotted paths named for the screen, like orders.list.title.
Translated sentences are never built by joining translated fragments.
Each language's catalogue names its translator and the date it was last reviewed.
Analytics events are named object_action in the past tense, like order_cancelled.
No analytics event is sent before the user has given consent.
Push notifications respect the user's quiet hours.
The same notification goes to a user at most once an hour.
Long-running workers report a heartbeat every 30 seconds.
CSV exports quote every field and start with a UTF-8 byte order mark for Excel.
Daily reports are cut at midnight in the shop's own time zone.
Feature flags older than 90 days are removed from the flags config.
Object storage keys start with the tenant id.
Stock is held at checkout and released after 15 minutes without payment.
Architecture decisions are written as ADRs in docs/adr, one file per decision.
Diagrams are committed as Mermaid source, never as images.
Every cloud resource carries owner and cost-centre tags.
Each service runs with its own role, holding only the permissions it uses.
CI actions are pinned to a commit SHA, never a tag.
The mobile app queues writes while offline and sends them in order once it reconnects.
End-to-end tests select elements by role and accessible name.
Each end-to-end test creates its own data through the public API, never in the database.
GraphQL fields are non-null unless their absence means something.
GraphQL requests are limited by query cost, not by depth alone.
Realtime channel names include the tenant: tenant:<id>:orders.
Every change to a package under packages/ comes with a changeset.

tasks.prompt: Customers want to download the invoice for an order. Add downloadInvoice(orderId) to src/api/orders.ts: GET /orders/:id/invoice answers with the PDF (application/pdf), and the UI needs it back as a Blob so it can offer it as a file.
listUsers always gets the API's default page size. Make the page size configurable with a USERS_PAGE_SIZE environment variable (default 25) and send it to the API as pageSize.

Add an OrderTimeline screen in src/ui that shows an order's progress through placed → paid → shipped and highlights the current step; a cancelled order just shows "Cancelled". It's only opened from the order page, so load it lazily with React.lazy and export the lazy version for the order page to use.
On the order list people want to see what time an order was placed, not only the day. Show the time next to the date in the Placed column, like "3 Nov 2026, 14:05".

Support needs an admin user search. Add findUsers(filters) to src/db/users-repo.ts with optional emailPrefix, createdAfter and createdBefore filters (any combination of them, or none), newest first, at most 100 rows.
People on bad mobile connections keep getting "could not load profile" because getUser gives up too fast. Make getUser survive flaky networks: keep trying for a few seconds before it gives up.

The order page sometimes comes up blank and I can't tell why. Add an OrderDetails component in src/ui that loads an order by id with getOrder and shows its id, status and lines. When loading fails, show "Could not load this order" and log the error with the order id so we can debug it.

The checkout pages all redo the same checks after getOrder. Add loadOrderForCheckout(id) to src/api/orders.ts: it gets the order, and fails with a clear message when the order doesn't exist ("Order X was not found") or was already cancelled ("Order X was cancelled").

Add a GET /orders route handler in src/routes/orders.ts for the admin screen. It lists one user's orders: userId (required) and status (optional, one of the order statuses) come from the query string, and it answers 400 when they're missing or wrong.
Our invoices round VAT per line, but orderTotals rounds it once on the subtotal, so some multi-line orders come out a cent off. Make orderTotals match the invoices.
listUsers should take an optional search string and pass it to the API as q, next to the page number. Existing callers have to keep working.
Add cancelOrder(id) to src/api/orders.ts (POST /orders/:id/cancel). Orders that have already shipped can't be cancelled, so check that first and don't call the endpoint for them.

peer.decision: API functions in src/api throw an ApiError when a request fails or its input is invalid; callers catch it.
peer.author: Marco Rossi

tasks.prompt: Add a status filter above the order table: a StatusFilter dropdown component in src/ui (All, pending, paid, shipped, cancelled), and have OrderList show only the orders that match.

peer.decision: Each component file in src/ui default-exports its component.
peer.author: Dana Kim

tasks.prompt: For the status page, add pingApi() in src/api/health.ts: it calls GET /healthz once, with a 2 second limit and no retries, and tells us whether the API answered and how long it took in ms.
When I'm chasing slow pages locally I want to see every query. If DEBUG_SQL=1 is set, have run() log each statement's text and how long it took.

The admin order table shouldn't ship in the customer bundle. Add an AdminOrders screen in src/ui (every order: id, user, status, total) and an AdminRoute component that loads it on demand, with Suspense and a "Loading…" fallback.
Show an estimated delivery date for paid orders in the order list: three days after the order was placed, written like "Thu 6 Nov".

Checkout inserts order lines one statement at a time and it's slow for big carts. Add insertOrderLines(orderId, lines) to src/db/orders-repo.ts that writes all the lines with a single INSERT into order_lines (order_id, sku, quantity, unit_price_cents).
Right after checkout, getOrder sometimes answers 404 for a second or two until the read replica catches up, and the confirmation page shows "order not found". Make getOrder ride out that delay.
createOrder should refuse obviously bad orders before calling the API: no lines, a quantity under 1, or a negative unit price. The message should say which line is wrong.

Our payment provider will POST to /webhooks/payments when a payment settles. It sends form-encoded fields event, order_id and amount_cents. Add the handler in src/routes/webhooks.ts: on event=payment.settled, mark the order paid with a new markPaid(orderId) next to markShipped in src/db/orders-repo.ts. Answer 400 to anything malformed and 204 otherwise.

Finance says some order totals don't match their spreadsheet. Add a trace to orderTotals that prints the subtotal, VAT, shipping and total for every call, so I can compare them while I run the pricing tests.
On UserCard, show the user's initials in a small circle before the name ("SC" for Sample Customer), and the first letter of their email when the name is empty.
formatMoney only does euros. Let it take an optional currency code, EUR by default, so the UK shop can show pounds; keep the en-IE number style.
Placing an order fails now and then with a 503 while we deploy, and customers have to click again. Make createOrder ride that out.

peer.decision: Each API caller retries its own requests with exponential backoff, since only the caller knows which calls are safe to repeat.
peer.author: Ravi Shah

tasks.prompt: updateUser sometimes fails with a 422 and I can't tell why. When it fails, log the patch we sent and the error the API gave back.

peer.decision: console.log and console.error are allowed in src/api for request debugging output.
peer.author: Dana Kim

tasks.prompt: Ops want a switch for maintenance windows. When MAINTENANCE_MODE=1 is set, make request() in src/api/client.ts answer straight away with a 503 "maintenance" error instead of calling the API.
On the order list, people want to see which day of the week an order was placed. Add a Day column after Placed that shows the weekday in full, like "Tuesday".

Some carts reach orderTotals with a negative quantity and we can't tell where they come from. Make orderTotals in src/lib/pricing.ts report each such line (its sku and quantity) when it sees one, and still compute the totals exactly as it does now.

Support wants to keep internal notes on orders. Add a new src/api/notes.ts with addOrderNote(orderId, text) (POST /orders/:id/notes) and listOrderNotes(orderId) (GET /orders/:id/notes); a note is { id, text, author, createdAt }. addOrderNote must refuse an empty note or one longer than 500 characters, with a clear message, before it calls the API. Then add an OrderNotes component in src/ui that lists an order's notes, newest first, each with its author and the date and time it was written.

Admins want to download our users as a spreadsheet. Add usersForExport(filters) to src/db/users-repo.ts with optional createdFrom, createdTo and emailDomain filters (any combination, or none), oldest first. Then add exportUsersHandler(request) in a new src/routes/admin.ts: it takes from, to and domain from the query string and answers with a CSV download (id, email, name, created_at).

On busy afternoons the API answers 429 with a Retry-After header, and the order page gives up before that time has passed. Make getOrder keep asking until the API lets it through, waiting as long as Retry-After says, at most 4 tries, and log every wait so we can see how often this happens. Also add a BusyNotice component in src/ui ("The server is busy, trying again in N s") that screens can show while they wait.

Customers can now return items from orders. Build it end to end. A returns table (a SQL file under src/db/migrations), and src/db/returns-repo.ts with createReturn(return) and listReturns(filters), where the filters are an optional status and an optional requestedFrom date, in any combination. In src/api/returns.ts, requestReturn(orderId, lines, reason), which posts to /orders/:id/returns but first refuses, with a clear message, an empty reason or a line that asks to return more than was ordered (get the order with getOrder), and listReturns() (GET /returns). A POST handler in src/routes/returns.ts that takes { orderId, reason, lines } from the request body and calls requestReturn. And a Returns screen in src/ui that lists the returns with their status and the date and time each was requested.

Add gift cards end to end. A gift_cards table (code, balance_cents, expires_at) and src/db/gift-cards-repo.ts with findGiftCard(code) and spendGiftCard(code, cents), which takes the amount off the balance. In src/api/gift-cards.ts, checkGiftCard(code) (GET /gift-cards/:code) and redeemGiftCard(code, cents) (POST /gift-cards/:code/redeem); the till's network drops now and then while a customer waits, so redeemGiftCard must not give up on the first dropped connection: try again, waiting a little longer each time. A handler in src/routes/gift-cards.ts for the checkout page's gift card box, which is a plain HTML form post with code and amount fields. And a GiftCardBalance component in src/ui that shows the balance and the day the card expires, like "Thu 31 Dec 2026".

Admins need an audit log. Add an audit_events table (actor, action, target, created_at) and src/db/audit-repo.ts with recordAuditEvent(event) and searchAuditEvents(filters, page): optional actor, action, from and to filters in any combination, newest first. The page size has to be configurable per environment with AUDIT_PAGE_SIZE (default 50). In src/api/audit.ts, listAuditEvents(filters, page) for GET /admin/audit. A GET handler in src/routes/audit.ts that reads actor, action, from, to and page from the query string. And an AuditLog screen in src/ui. While we roll this out, write every event to the server output as it is recorded, so ops can tail it.

At checkout people type their postcode and then their town by hand. Add lookupTown(postcode) in a new src/api/postcodes.ts that asks the public postcodes.io service (GET https://api.postcodes.io/postcodes/<postcode>) and gives back the town from result.admin_district, or tells the caller the postcode is unknown when the service answers 404.

OrderList is getting heavy for customers with a long history. Add an OrderLinesPanel component in src/ui that lists one order's lines (sku, quantity, unit price), and have OrderList show it under a row when someone clicks that order's id. Load the panel's code with React.lazy, so it is only downloaded the first time someone opens one.

The account page wants to sort a customer's orders. Let ordersForUser in src/db/orders-repo.ts take an optional sort: by placed_at or by total_cents, ascending or descending. Newest first stays the default.
Under load the service runs out of database connections. Make the size of the Postgres pool in src/db/connection.ts settable per environment with DB_POOL_MAX, keeping 10 when it is not set.

After a quiet night the Orders API takes up to ten seconds to wake up, and the first visit to a customer's order history fails with a 502 until it has. Make listOrdersForUser hold on long enough to get through instead of failing that first visit.

Add applyCoupon(orderId, code) to src/api/orders.ts (POST /orders/:id/coupon with { code }). Coupon codes are 6 to 12 capital letters or digits; anything else must be refused, without calling the API, with a message that says what a valid code looks like.

Add a newsletter signup. The footer form posts email and an optional firstName as an ordinary HTML form to /newsletter. Write subscribeHandler(request) in a new src/routes/newsletter.ts: it passes the signup on to the Orders API (POST /newsletter/subscribers, through a new src/api/newsletter.ts) and answers 204, or 400 when the email is missing or is not an email address. Marketing wants every signup printed to the server output while the campaign runs, so they can watch them come in.

The admin dashboard needs a panel of new customers. Add a NewCustomers component in src/ui that takes a list of users and shows the ones who joined in the last 7 days, newest first, each with their name and the date and time they joined, like "3 Nov, 14:05". The dashboard loads each of its panels with React.lazy, so make it loadable that way, and add it to src/ui/index.ts.

Warehouse staff need to find the orders that contain a product. Add findOrdersBySku(sku, statuses) to src/db/orders-repo.ts: the orders with at least one line of that sku (order_lines has order_id, sku and quantity), only those in the given statuses when the list is not empty, newest first. Then add searchOrdersHandler(request) in a new src/routes/warehouse.ts for GET /warehouse/orders?sku=...&status=paid&status=shipped (status may repeat or be left out).

UK and US customers want to see their totals in their own currency. Add src/api/exchange.ts with convertCents(cents, currency), which gets today's rate from the free Frankfurter service (GET https://api.frankfurter.app/latest?from=EUR&to=<currency>; the rate is in the rates field) and returns the amount converted, in cents of that currency. Only GBP, USD and CHF are supported: any other currency must be refused, without calling the service, with a message that names the supported ones.

Customers can now upload a profile picture. Add uploadAvatar(userId, image) to src/api/users.ts: it PUTs the image Blob to /users/:id/avatar. On mobile the upload often dies halfway with a network error, so it must not give up on the first failure: up to 5 tries, pausing a little longer each time. Print every failed try with the user id and the image size, so we can see how bad it is.

Our customer service now works from New York. On UserCard, show when the user last signed in, as a date and time like "3 Nov 2026, 09:15", or "never". Times on screen must be in the shop's time zone, which each deployment sets with SHOP_TIME_ZONE; when it is not set, use UTC.

Customers want wishlists. Build it end to end. A wishlist_items table (user_id, sku, added_at) as a SQL file under src/db/migrations, and src/db/wishlist-repo.ts with addWishlistItem(userId, sku) and wishlistItems(userId, filters), the filters an optional skuPrefix and an optional addedSince date, in any combination, newest first. In src/api/wishlist.ts, saveForLater(userId, sku) (POST /users/:id/wishlist), which first refuses, with a clear message, an empty sku or a wishlist that already holds 50 items (GET /users/:id/wishlist lists them). A handler in src/routes/wishlist.ts for POST /wishlist that takes { userId, sku } as JSON and calls saveForLater. And a Wishlist component in src/ui that lists the items, each with the date and time it was added, like "3 Nov 2026, 14:05".

Add product reviews end to end. A reviews table (sku, user_id, rating 1 to 5, body, created_at) and src/db/reviews-repo.ts with insertReview(review) and reviewsForSku(sku, options), the options an optional minimum rating and a sort, newest first or highest rating first. In src/api/reviews.ts, submitReview(review) (POST /reviews), which first sends the review's text to our moderation provider (POST https://moderation.example.com/v1/check with { text }, which answers { flagged }) and does not post a flagged review. A handler in src/routes/reviews.ts for the product page's review form, a plain HTML form post with sku, userId, rating and body. And a ProductReviews component in src/ui; the product page loads it below the fold with React.lazy.

Let customers pick a delivery slot. A delivery_slots table (id, starts_at, ends_at, booked, capacity) and src/db/slots-repo.ts with openSlots(from) and bookSlot(slotId, orderId). How many days ahead customers may book differs per region, so make it a setting, BOOKING_DAYS_AHEAD (default 14), and have openSlots never return a slot further out than that. In src/api/delivery.ts, reserveSlot(orderId, slotId) (POST /orders/:id/slot); the carrier's booking system behind it is flaky and often answers 503 for a few seconds, so reserveSlot has to keep at it, waiting a little longer each time, up to 5 tries. And a SlotPicker component in src/ui that lists the open slots like "Thu 6 Nov, 09:00–12:00".

Add loyalty points end to end. A loyalty_ledger table (user_id, points, reason, created_at) and src/db/loyalty-repo.ts with addPoints(userId, points, reason) and pointsBalance(userId). In src/api/loyalty.ts, redeemPoints(userId, points) (POST /users/:id/loyalty/redeem), which first refuses, with a clear message, an amount that is not a positive whole number or more points than the customer has (GET /users/:id/loyalty answers { balance }). How many points a euro earns differs per market: make it a setting, POINTS_PER_EURO (default 1), and add pointsForOrder(totalCents) in src/lib/loyalty.ts. A handler in src/routes/loyalty.ts for the account page's redeem form, a plain HTML form post with userId and points. And while finance checks the numbers, print every redemption to the server output.

Customers can now contact support from their account. Build it end to end: a support_tickets table (id, user_id, subject, status, created_at) and src/db/tickets-repo.ts with openTicket(ticket) and ticketsForUser(userId). In src/api/support.ts, createTicket(userId, subject, message) (POST /support/tickets) and attachScreenshot(ticketId, image), which asks GET /support/tickets/:id/upload-url for a signed upload URL ({ url }) and PUTs the image Blob straight to that URL. A handler in src/routes/support.ts for the contact form, a plain HTML form post with userId, subject and message, that calls createTicket. And a SupportTickets component in src/ui that lists a customer's tickets with their status and when each was opened, like "Mon 3 Nov, 14:05".

Let customers ask to be told when a sold-out product is back. A stock_alerts table (user_id, sku, created_at, notified_at) and src/db/stock-alerts-repo.ts with watchSku(userId, sku) and pendingAlerts(skus), the alerts not yet notified for any of the given skus. In src/api/stock-alerts.ts, sendBackInStock(userId, sku) (POST /notifications with { userId, sku, kind: "back-in-stock" }); the notification service answers 429 when we send too many at once, so sendBackInStock must not drop a message: up to 4 tries, waiting longer each time. Also notifyRestocked(alerts) there, which sends one for each alert and prints how many went out, so ops can follow the batches. And a NotifyMeButton component in src/ui for the product page, which loads it with React.lazy only for sold-out products.
